newsitem.title: FRANCE: French growth may be faster than forecast - govt.
newsitem.headline: French growth may be faster than forecast - govt.

text.p: French growth this year may be faster than the 2.3 percent rise officially forecast, the finance ministry said on Wednesday.

After a review of economic forecasts made last year for the 1997 budget, it confirmed that it was sticking to its forecast of 2.3 percent growth this year and 2.8 percent next year after 1.3 percent in 1996.
But it said in a statement it was being deliberately cautious in its forecast.
"It has been assumed here that the improvement in monetary and financial conditions will not be felt fully until 1998. But an earlier and stronger acceleration in growth is quite possible," it said.
Growth would pick up to a year-on-year rate of around three percent by the end of this year, it said.
Recovery would be led first by external demand and an end to destocking, and then slowly build up, helped by a revival in investment and in internal demand.
It said employment would pick up from the first half of 1997 onwards. Over the full year, there would be 120,000 to 140,000 net new jobs created in the non-farm market sector.
In 1998, an acceleration in growth would create 220,000 to 250,000 additional jobs.

The statement made no forecast on the unemployment rate, which reached a record 12.8 percent in February. Job creation in recent months has so far failed to outstrip a rise in the active working population.
It repeated that the total budget deficit would be reduced to three percent of gross domestic product in 1997 and to 2.8 percent of GDP in 1998 from 4.1 percent last year.
